name: Ruined Arch

detectability.signature: Spatial displacement field detectable as a localized absence on mass-density scanners, bordered by a thin shell of elevated gravitometric readings

proximity: Sensor returns become unreliable as spatial metrics distort near the boundary, showing objects at incorrect distances
Navigation systems report contradictory position fixes, with internal and external references diverging by increasing margins
contact: Vessels crossing the boundary experience a disorienting spatial inversion, with interior dimensions momentarily appearing larger or smaller than they should be
All external sensor contact is lost upon entry; the pocket's interior is dimensionally isolated from surrounding space
Communication signals cannot penetrate the boundary in either direction
prolonged_exposure: Extended habitation within the pocket produces cumulative spatial disorientation that persists for days after departure
Equipment calibrated to standard spatial metrics gradually loses accuracy, requiring full recalibration upon exit
Some crews report a persistent psychological unease described as the sense of being in a room with no doors

age: The pocket dimension itself may be of any age, but the boundary structure shows engineering signatures estimated at 50,000 to 80,000 years old
phenomena: The boundary shell is marked by a ring of faint gravitometric distortion that, when mapped in three dimensions, traces the outline of an enormous archway, most of which has apparently collapsed or degraded
The pocket interior is a sphere of perfect emptiness, containing no matter, no radiation, and no background energy of any kind
Objects left inside the pocket remain in a state of near-perfect preservation, experiencing negligible entropy
A series of geometric indentations on the interior surface of the boundary correspond to no known language or mathematical notation but are clearly artificial in origin
hazards: Total communication blackout within the pocket makes rescue operations extremely difficult
The boundary crossing induces momentary spatial disorientation that has caused navigational accidents
The artificial origin implies a creator civilization whose intentions and potential safeguards remain unknown
opportunities: The pocket's near-zero entropy environment makes it an unparalleled preservation vault for sensitive materials, artifacts, or data
The engineering principles behind the boundary structure could revolutionize spatial manipulation technology if understood
The geometric inscriptions represent a potential first-contact artifact of immense xenoarchaeological value
known_incidents: The survey probe Threadneedle entered the pocket in 3189 and transmitted no data for 47 days before being recovered at the boundary exit point, its internal clock showing only 47 days had passed but its crew of three reporting no memory of the intervening time
description: Ruined Arch is invisible to the naked eye and nearly so to standard instrumentation. It exists as a pocket of folded space, an interior without an exterior, accessible only through a boundary region that registers on mass-density scanners as a thin shell of gravitometric irregularity. When that shell is mapped in full, its contours describe the remnants of an enormous archway, roughly 2,800 meters at its widest span, most of which has degraded into fragmentary readings. The intact portion still functions as an entry point into the void beyond.

Inside the pocket, there is nothing. Not the nothing of deep space, which is still filled with radiation and stray particles, but a more fundamental emptiness. Sensors return zeroes across every spectrum. The interior is a sealed volume approximately 3,100 kilometers in radius, spherical, featureless, and profoundly silent. Objects brought inside experience negligible entropy, their molecular bonds undisturbed by any external force. It is, in the most literal sense, a vault with nothing in it.

The artificial nature of the Ruined Arch is not in serious dispute. The boundary structure's gravitometric profile shows regularities that cannot arise naturally, and the geometric inscriptions on the pocket's interior surface are unmistakably deliberate. The builder civilization, whoever they were, operated on a scale and with a mastery of spatial physics that dwarfs current capabilities. Some researchers have speculated that the pocket was a storage facility, emptied long ago. Others suggest it was a sealed environment, a quarantine chamber or a prison, and that whatever it once contained was removed or escaped.

Ruined Arch is currently classified as a protected xenoarchaeological site, with access restricted to licensed research expeditions. A small orbital habitat, Keystone Station, maintains position near the boundary and serves as a staging area for survey teams. The most pressing current question involves the inscriptions: a recent computational analysis suggested they may encode spatial coordinates, potentially pointing to other pocket dimensions or to the builders' point of origin. If confirmed, this would transform the Ruined Arch from a curiosity into a roadmap.
